subject: Pilot runway smoothing & feature-gate credits
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Liam Gray <liam.gray@olivesys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot runway smoothing & feature-gate credits

Hi Liam —

Great demo yesterday — thanks for the honest feedback on the feature-gate cadence and the spike in inference during the A/B ramp. Based on the usage profile you showed, we want to propose a small pilot amendment that smooths the runway for you while keeping the economics simple. High-level: 

- Add a one-time 2-week runway smoothing window (extend pilot by 14 calendar days) tied to the feature gate launch so you aren’t penalized for concentrated traffic during ramp.
- Provide a 25% credit on overage tokens incurred during the smoothing window (applies only to tokens above the original pilot cap).
- If Olive decides to convert to a Dedicated commitment within 30 days of the smoothing window end, we’ll apply an additional credit equal to 10% of the smoothing-window billed amount toward the first month.

I’ve attached a short amendment draft and a simple usage-estimates sheet so procurement can see the math. If this looks reasonable, Ben can send a redline-ready version for legal and we can route to DocuSign.

Questions for you: does procurement need a fixed-cost conversion path instead of a percent credit? Any internal approvals needed to sign an addendum quickly?

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-poc-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF: 2 pages)
Attachment: olive-usage-estimates.xlsx (XLSX: sample month-by-month projection)

From: Liam Gray <liam.gray@olivesys.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@olivesys.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway smoothing & feature-gate credits

Ava —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the concrete wording. A couple of notes from our side: 

1) We prefer credits expressed as fixed USD amounts for SOWs that cross quarters (makes forecasting easier). Could you translate the 25% overage credit into a not-to-exceed USD cap?
2) We will need the amendment to be explicit about which model variants the credit applies to (we only plan to use the r-instruct-large and r-chat-medium variants during the gate).
3) Legal will want a short shelf-life on conversion credits (30 days is fine).

If you can send a redline that has both (A) a percent option and (B) an equivalent fixed-dollar alternative, procurement can review faster.

Thanks —
Liam
Head of Engineering | Olive Systems
liam.gray@olivesys.com

On Tue, Sep 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Great demo yesterday — thanks for the honest feedback...

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam Gray <liam.gray@olivesys.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot runway smoothing & feature-gate credits (draft alternatives)

Liam —

Thanks for the guidance. I’ve put together two concrete amendment options (see summary below) and attached a clean draft you can forward to legal. Short summary: 

Option A — Percent-based (keeps flexibility)
- 25% credit on overage tokens during the 14-day smoothing window
- No not-to-exceed cap
- Applies to r-instruct-large and r-chat-medium as specified

Option B — Fixed USD cap (procurement-friendly)
- Equivalent fixed credit: $18,000 not-to-exceed credit to offset overages for the 14-day window (based on your mid-range estimate in the usage sheet)
- If actual overage cost is below $18,000 we’ll credit the actual amount only (no double-payment)

Additional notes:
- Conversion credit: 10% of smoothing-window billed amount applied to first Dedicated month (30-day shelf life).
- Legal: I added a specific model-variant appendix and a short exhibit with the usage assumptions we discussed.

If Olive picks Option B we can lock in the cap in the redline and move to signature. If you’d like, we can also split the not-to-exceed cap across billing buckets (e.g., $10k for inference, $8k for embeddings) — tell me preference.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: redwood-poc-amendment-draft.pdf (updated with both options)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam Gray <liam.gray@olivesys.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot runway smoothing & feature-gate credits — next steps

Liam —

Appreciate the quick review. From Redwood’s side we’re happy to proceed with Option B (the $18k not-to-exceed cap) to simplify procurement and speed signature. A couple of procedural items: 

- We’ll prepare a redline that calls out the model variants and attaches the usage assumption exhibit.
- I’ll kick off the DocuSign route after legal signs off — should be a same-day turnaround once we get the procurement PO number.
- Please confirm who will be the signatory on Olive’s end (procurement@olivesys.com is fine if they’re authorized).

Ben — can you drop the redline by EOD so I can push to Legal? Liam — once you confirm the signatory and whether you want the cap split into buckets I’ll route the package.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
